chunks: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad narrated from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Kindness [to parents] increases one's lifespan and charity given secretly calms the Lord's wrath.

key_terms.الْبِرُّ: Kindness, piety, or filial duty (often specifically to parents)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of secret charity and kindness to parents in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) links 'al-Birr'—specifically emphasizing filial piety in this chapter—to the prolongation of life, a concept supported by Shia exegetes who view it as both physical longevity and spiritual vitality. The second part highlights the efficacy of 'sadaqat al-sirr' (secret charity) in averting divine wrath, reflecting the Shia emphasis on sincerity (ikhlas) and the removal of hidden sins. This teaching underscores the dual benefit of righteous deeds: enhancing one's worldly existence and securing spiritual peace through concealed acts of worship.
